correctness.rationale: Dhar burning gives \(3^k\) recurrent configurations in each sink case. With the peripheral sink, every state is exactly one of three gate heights times three choices per other triangle, which is proved by the threshold-burning order. Each toppling vector in the finite gate/local-state table yields a stable recurrent representative in the correct Laplacian class; uniqueness of recurrent representatives gives the exact odometer. Coefficient counts sum to \(2k\cdot3^k\); the weak limit counts nine equally likely source types. Independently implemented exhaustive Dhar/greedy and analytic-template/parallel-wave programs agree for \(1\le k\le7\) and \(1\le k\le8\) respectively; finite checking is not invoked as the all-size proof.

originality.rationale: The strongest inspected source for principal avalanche enumeration, Austin et al. (2016), provides the general observable and exact evaluated families (trees, cycles, wheels and complete graphs), but no friendship-graph two-sink polynomial. Gauthier (2011) concerns first-wave cell masses on growing expanded-cactus balls, neither this fixed finite cactus nor the complete number-of-topplings/sink-loss observable. The accessible closely related published records concern graph invariants other than the sandpile, or a different prism/bipyramid sink comparison. The new result derives explicit joint polynomials, an exact finite-size extensive-avalanche law and a three-atom limit not supplied by the cited general framework. This is a qualified literature comparison, not an assertion of proof of global priority.
residual_risks: A less-accessible, unindexed treatment of sandpiles on windmill or general finite cactus graphs could contain an equivalent two-sink coefficient formula.
General graph deletion-contraction or composition identities might allow a short further derivation from earlier general theory; no direct evaluated equivalent was established.
No independent historical-priority validation has been performed.

value.rationale: Avalanche statistics are mathematically meaningful transport observables that are not determined by the sandpile group. This result classifies both inequivalent sink orbits on a natural infinite family, quantifies an extreme change from at most two topplings to \(4k+1\), and produces exact macroscopic avalanche probabilities and a nontrivial weak limit. This distinguishes absorbing geometry from algebraic critical-group invariance in a way not contained in a general assertion of sink dependence. Its unbounded hub degree is explicitly acknowledged; no unjustified universality claim is made.
